title: Infra GPU Fleet, Capacity, IaC & CI/CD Operational Playbook
author: Lena Chen
body:
Summary:

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's operational guidance for the GPU fleet, capacity planning, cloud accounts & networking, Terraform/IaC modules, CI/CD pipelines and day-2 runbooks. It is intended for infra engineers, SREs, and platform owners responsible for procuring, provisioning, and operating inference capacity across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Goals:
- Provide a single source of truth for capacity decisions, IaC patterns, and CI/CD best practices.
- Reduce mean time to repair (MTTR) for infra incidents affecting GPU capacity and networking.
- Ensure consistent Terraform module usage across cloud accounts and regions.
- Surface operational runbooks for common scenarios (OOMs, degraded GPU network, instance drift, rolling kernel updates).

Scope:
- GPU fleet (on-prem and cloud): node types, sizing guidance, GPU profiles, and utilization targets.
- Capacity planning: forecast cadence, buffer policy, burst capacity and preemptible vs reserved mix.
- Cloud accounts & networking: account structure, VPC design, peering, and inter-region considerations.
- Terraform/IaC modules: canonical modules, patterns for multi-account reuse, policies, and testing strategy.
- CI/CD & build: pipeline layout, automated canaries, module testing, and release gating.
- Runbooks & Day-2 ops: incident response, upgrades, rollbacks, and oncall handoff checklist.

Ownership and Roles:
- Infra Platform Team (primary): ownership of Terraform modules, CI/CD pipelines, and global GPU capacity policies.
- GPU Fleet SREs: monitoring, incident response, capacity alerts, and on-call rotation.
- Cloud Accounts Team: account hygiene, billing isolation, and cross-account networking.
- Model Serving / Runtime Team: coordinates kernel-level changes and model-compatibility matrix for GPU types.

High-level Architecture Overview:
- Cluster topology: GPU nodes grouped into capacity pools by region + tier (hosted/dedicated/private). Each pool has an autoscaling controller, batch scheduler, and KV cache service endpoints.
- Network segmentation: management VPCs (control plane) are separated from runtime VPCs (inference traffic). Cross-account VPC peering or Transit Gateway used for Dedicated customer attachments.
- IaC pipeline: monorepo for terraform modules (modules/), environment repos for account-level composition (env-prod/, env-staging/), and a centralized module registry (internal).

Capacity Planning & Policy:
- Targets:
  - Average GPU utilization target (inference tokens): 45-60% sustained per-pool to balance cost vs latency.
  - Burst headroom: maintain 20% spare capacity to absorb demand spikes; prioritized in autoscaler policy.
  - Cold-start SLA: 95th percentile provisioning time for an additional 10% capacity < 90s in cloud regions with reserved capacity.
- Forecast cadence:
  1. Weekly: short-term demand trends and immediate scale actions.
  2. Monthly: capacity runway for next 90 days; update reserved vs on-demand mix.
  3. Quarterly: commit sizing for Dedicated (customer contracts) and procurement planning for on-prem expansion.
- Buffer policy:
  - Maintain a configurable buffer per-pool (default 20%). Buffer consumption alarms trigger a capacity review runbook.
  - Preferred mitigation order: autoscale warm nodes -> spill to lower-cost model variant -> request immediate reserved allocation from capacity team -> controlled shedding for non-critical jobs.

GPU Types, Profiles & Placement:
- Standard profiles (examples):
  - a100-80gb: high-throughput large-context models (LLM-XXL), preferred for Dedicated and private deployments.
  - a100-40gb: general purpose large-model serving, balance of cost/throughput.
  - h100-80gb: experimental kernel optimizations, use in canary pools only.
  - g5-24gb: cost-efficient for small-medium models and embeddings.
- Placement rules:
  - Latency-sensitive routes prefer nodes in smallest network hop region and dedicated pool.
  - Heavy KV-cache workloads colocate with the serving pods to reduce cross-host network egress.

Cloud Accounts & Networking Guidance:
- Account structure:
  - org-root -> billing -> shared-services (IAM, logging, CIP) -> infra-prod -> infra-staging -> customer-dedicated-{id}.
  - Least privilege access enforced via cross-account roles.
- VPC design:
  - Management VPCs host control plane services; runtime VPCs host GPU clusters.
  - Subnets: separate subnets for GPU nodes, NAT, and management traffic.
  - Use Transit Gateway or cloud-native equivalent for multi-region Dedicated connectivity; prefer encrypted peering.
- Network limits and mitigation:
  - Track per-region ENI and IP address exhaustion metrics.
  - Use IP address pools and secondary CIDR when scaling large clusters.
  - For high egress workloads, provision dedicated egress NAT gateways per-cluster to avoid cross-team contention.

Terraform / IaC Modules & Patterns:
- Canonical modules (monorepo/modules):
  - module/gpu_cluster: provisions node groups, autoscaler config, and safety hooks.
  - module/networking: VPC, subnets, route tables, and TGW attachments.
  - module/cloud_accounts: account bootstrap (roles, SCPs, logging).
  - module/iam_roles: centralized role patterns for cross-account access.
  - module/observability: metrics exporters, log sinks, alerting resources.
- Module usage rules:
  - Modules must be immutable by tag: release tag pattern vYYYY.MM.patch. No direct trunk references in env repos.
  - All changes require: unit tests (terraform-compliance / tflint), integration plan check (plan preview with drift detection), and a staged apply in staging before prod.
  - Policy-as-code: use gate policies (Sentinel / OPA) to enforce approved instance types and restrict public CIDR exposures.
- Testing strategy:
  - Unit: tflint + terraform validate in PR.
  - Integration: terratest or kitchen-terraform in ephemeral cloud accounts in CI with teardown.
  - Plan checks: automated drift detection job nightly that notifies owners.

CI/CD & Build Practices:
- Repo layout:
  - infra-modules/ (all modules), env-overlays/ (per-account compositions), pipelines/ (shared pipeline templates).
- Pipeline stages (canonical):
  1. Lint & static checks (tflint, checkov).
  2. Unit tests (terraform validate, module unit tests).
  3. Plan (in temporary environment with mocked state).
  4. Manual approval for prod plan apply (two-person rule for gpu_cluster module changes).
  5. Apply with canary: create canary node pool with 1-2 nodes, wait 30m validation window (monitoring and perf tests), then scale remainder if stable.
- Secrets & artifact management:
  - Use centralized secrets manager (KMS + secret store). No secrets in terraform state.
  - CI runners assume ephemeral roles with least privilege for each pipeline.

Runbooks & Common Incident Playbooks:
- Incident: GPU node OOM / kernel panic (high severity)
  1. Triage: identify affected pool via cluster-metrics dashboard (tag: gpu-errors).
 2. Run: kubectl get nodes -o wide; check node-level dmesg and system logs (ELK/Cloud Logging).
 3. Isolate: cordon & drain node; mark any suspicious AMI/kernel changes.
 4. Restore: replace with new node from healthy image; if repeated failures, rollback kernel or image via module version rollback.
 5. Postmortem: create incident postmortem within 72 hours; include root cause, impact, and remediation steps.
- Incident: Network egress saturation to external storage (medium)
  1. Identify flows via VPC Flow Logs and Net Observability dashboards.
 2. Throttle or redirect to internal cache if available.
 3. If NAT gateway overwhelmed, provision additional NAT capacity or move egress via dedicated egress nodes.
- Alerting thresholds (examples):
  - GPU memory error rate > 0.5% over 5m -> sev2.
  - Node provisioning queue length > 50 for 10m -> capacity review.
  - Drift detection: terraform drift > 2 resources changed in env -> oncall notify.

Day-2 Ops: Upgrades, Rollbacks, and Kernel Changes:
- Upgrade procedure (kernel/AMI):
  1. Create image and deploy to canary pool (1-2 nodes) in target region.
 2. Run service-level smoke tests and perf microbenchmarks (latency, p95 IO).
 3. Monitor for 6 hours (or configured validation window) before promoting.
 4. If issues arise, initiate rollback using module tag that references previous AMI.
- Rolling firmware / driver updates:
  - Validate compatibility with current runtime (serving-runtime team must sign off).
  - Stagger updates across availability zones and use health-based rollouts.

Monitoring, SLOs & Reporting:
- Key metrics:
  - GPU utilization (per-device), GPU memory pressure, kernel OOM counts, node replace rate, node provisioning time, and network egress rates.
- SLOs (infra-facing):
  - Fleet availability: 99.9% per-region for production pools (monthly).
  - Warm provisioning time (scale-up to 10%) p95 < 90s for reserved pools.
- Reporting:
  - Weekly capacity dashboard emailed to infra-owners with projection and buffer consumption.
  - Quarterly capacity review meeting with product and finance for Dedicated contract sizing.

Oncall Handoff Checklist (for GPU Fleet SREs):
- Current incidents (linked list).
- Recent capacity events and buffer usage.
- Pinned PRs / blocked infra changes.
- Next planned upgrades or kernel rollouts.
- Contact list: oncall rotation pager, infra lead, cloud accounts owner, serving runtime rep.

Appendix: Examples
- Terraform snippet (gpu_cluster module usage):
  ```hcl
  module "gpu_cluster_us_west" {
    source = "git::ssh://git@internal/redwood/infra-modules.git//modules/gpu_cluster?ref=v2025.11.1"

    region             = "us-west-2"
    instance_type      = "a100-40gb"
    desired_capacity   = 20
    min_capacity       = 6
    max_capacity       = 60
    autoscaler_config  = { target_utilization = 0.55, buffer = 0.2 }
    tags               = { team = "runtime" environment = "prod" }
  }
  ```

- CI pipeline snippet (canonical steps):
  ```yaml
  jobs:
    - name: lint
      run: tflint .
    - name: validate
      run: terraform validate
    - name: plan
      run: terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan
    - name: apply-canary
      when: manual
      run: terraform apply -target=module.gpu_cluster.canary plan.tfplan
  ```

Related pages and references:
- See: GPU capacity and infra runbook (link in related_pages).
- Terraform module registry: internal link in the console.
- Serving runtime compatibility matrix: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture/compatibility-matrix.

Maintenance and Governance:
- Module owners must rotate annually and keep module CHANGELOG up-to-date.
- All infra PRs touching gpu_cluster or networking modules require two approvers including one SRE.
- Monthly housekeeping job: identify stale images, unused IP reservations, and untagged resources; automated cleanup with two-week grace period.

Contacts for escalation:
